pillar_reactions.evidence: Checked the structure back to confirm he had understood: 'So, if I understood correctly, it's three, four days a week, the training, and every day, five to 15 minutes mobility exercises.' Then confirmed the timing was flexible before agreeing: 'Yeah, I get it.'

The only pillar he pushed back on, and he did it twice. Before the presentation: 'because my life is very demanding, I don't think I can do, I can fast for a very long time.' During it: 'I'm not sure about that... I have to see how it fits with my schedule, because most of the days I don't have time to come home and eat. I have to take something with me at the office or at the hospital.' The rep asserted the protocol would fit rather than showing how, and the prospect accepted on that assurance.

Understood and agreed with no questions: 'No, I think you covered everything very elegantly. I mean, I understood how you guys operate, and what's the philosophy of this whole process, and yeah, I understand it.' He had named feedback as his single biggest need earlier, so the pillar matched his own diagnosis.

anchors.raw: Mine would be 1k for six months.
anchors.note: A total of 1k across six months against $6,000, clarified explicitly as a total rather than a monthly figure. A six-fold gap, and the only one in the batch this large. Notably the $200 a month tier he was then offered totals roughly $1,200 over six months, which still exceeds his stated ceiling.

anchors.raw: It's worth a lot more than 6K, but it's just my budget. It's like that.
anchors.note: Complete value acceptance with zero capacity. The third prospect in this batch to accept the value above the asking price and still not buy — in this case the only one where the constraint is genuinely money rather than rate of return.

unmet_demand.want: One-to-one form feedback, which he named as the single thing he needs, at a price he can afford
unmet_demand.why_unmet: He answered the question 'what else would you want or need from Trevor?' with one word — 'Feedback' — and then 'If I'm doing the exercises correctly.' The only product inside his budget is the community, where form feedback is crowd-sourced and comes from 'Trevor, someone else from the team, or someone who's been doing kettlebells also for a very long time'. The one thing he needs is the one thing the affordable tier cannot guarantee.

unmet_demand.want: Nutrition that works around two hospital night shifts a week and days when he cannot get home to eat
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The protocol assumes an eating window and home cooking. He raised the conflict directly and the rep answered that Trevor would look into it, without showing how a shift roster is accommodated.
